intended_mind_change: Use actual drafting comparisons to revise one explanatory representation and one creative composition; keep demonstrated authored changes separate from human reception.
source_interpretation: 1: writing from scratch, all three drafts
user_override: Do not manufacture a bad first draft or pad prose merely to force the source cut ratio; do not claim unsupported universal facts about brains or prose.

plans.intended_mind_change: Replace my tentative aggregate-first explanatory plan if another structure makes the group-weight assumption explicit with fewer words.
plans.starting_judgment: I tentatively prefer opening with the aggregate reversal and explaining the two groups afterward; I have not compared complete skeletons. I already know rates can reverse under different mixtures, so discovering that theorem is not the claimed change.
plans.input: Fictional process A: easy 9/10, hard 10/100. Process B: easy 80/100, hard 0/10. Explain what these exact counts do and do not warrant. No causal assignment claim.
plans.purpose: Give a reader an exact, short explanation of an apparent rate contradiction and a usable comparison boundary.
plans.audience: A numerate general reader who can divide counts but has not seen this example.
plans.single_sentence: The aggregate compares different mixtures; a common mixture supports one comparison while neither table alone establishes causal superiority.

skeleton_alternatives.assessment: Strong surprise, but delays the denominator definition and makes a reader revise the first ranking.
Transparent derivation; four numerical frames before the actionable condition may make the note longer.

sequence: Separate arithmetic comparison from causal claim
skeleton_alternatives.assessment: Puts the decision boundary first while retaining an inspectable contradiction. Selected for actual drafting; efficiency remains to be measured.

selected_skeleton.job: Specify the question before the ranking
selected_skeleton.claim: An aggregate rate compares both performance and case mixture.
selected_skeleton.support: Each aggregate is a weighted mean of its group rates.
selected_skeleton.exit: A reader asks which mixture the comparison should describe.
selected_skeleton.counterargument: If the actual incoming mixtures are themselves the target, the aggregate remains a valid descriptive rate.

selected_skeleton.claim: A has higher observed success in each of two groups.
selected_skeleton.support: A easy9/10 hard10/100; B easy80/100 hard0/10.
selected_skeleton.exit: The reader can independently compute the two within-group comparisons.
selected_skeleton.counterargument: Observed rates alone need not describe causal effects.

selected_skeleton.claim: B has the higher overall observed rate in these samples.
selected_skeleton.support: A19/110 and B80/110; B has many more easy cases.
selected_skeleton.exit: No logical contradiction remains between aggregate and within-group rankings.

selected_skeleton.claim: At equal group weights the observed-rate comparison favors A.
selected_skeleton.exit: The reader can state the assumption behind this standardized comparison.
selected_skeleton.counterargument: Equal weighting is a chosen scenario, not a discovered population distribution.

selected_skeleton.claim: Neither summary alone proves that switching the process causes improvement.
selected_skeleton.support: The supplied fictional data specify no assignment mechanism or comparable counterfactual outcomes.
selected_skeleton.exit: A descriptive comparison is separated from a causal recommendation.

plans.intended_mind_change: Test whether changing a story from chronology to a decision-centered structure changes its authored interpretation while preserving its events and uncertainty.
plans.starting_judgment: I currently prefer the chronological version because it gives the letter its history before the reply. I intend the story to permit two readings of the request; I will not invent a failure to preserve that ambiguity just to earn a KEEP.
plans.input: Fictional Sela is drawing a coastal map away from home. Her father writes only: Tell us where you are. She has an unused return ticket. She sends a copy of her current map with her location marked and keeps the ticket. No reply arrives within the story. Do not settle what her father meant or predict his reaction.
plans.purpose: Produce a restrained short story about choosing a response under ambiguous relational intent.
plans.audience: An imagined adult fiction reader, simulated only; no real reader observation.
plans.single_sentence: Sela answers the words she received while leaving the larger question of return unresolved.

skeleton_alternatives.assessment: Preserves causal order and concrete objects; risks overexplaining background. Selected for draft1 to test the actual preferred baseline.

sequence: End with retained ticket and absent reply
skeleton_alternatives.assessment: Focuses the live choice with fewer background facts; may reduce the sense of elapsed distance.
Creates suspense but withholds the question after presenting the answer. Extra temporal reorder has no demonstrated benefit.

selected_skeleton.claim: Sela is mapping away from home.
selected_skeleton.support: Invented setting and current map in the supplied fiction.
selected_skeleton.exit: The reader locates the immediate scene.

selected_skeleton.claim: The short request does not settle whether return is wanted.
selected_skeleton.support: Exact five-word sentence and no later clarification.
selected_skeleton.exit: Both location request and implied invitation remain possible.
selected_skeleton.counterargument: A reader may prefer one pragmatic interpretation; the narrator must not certify it.

selected_skeleton.support: Unused ticket in the given event constraints.
selected_skeleton.exit: Remaining away is a choice with an available alternative.

selected_skeleton.claim: She sends a marked copy of the map.
selected_skeleton.exit: The reader sees what she does without a claim about its effect on her father.

selected_skeleton.claim: The ticket remains and no reply is observed.
selected_skeleton.exit: The action closes; relational interpretation remains open.

actual_mind_change: At the planning stage I changed the quantitative note from aggregate-first to comparison-first after comparing three skeletons. The story retains the credible chronological starting preference for an actual drafting test.
benefit: Candidate organization choices only; no completed prose or reader outcome yet.
organization: Both plans preserve rejected alternatives and the same explicit field set; the two writing targets and change criteria differ.
